definitions.gloss: coordinator; mediator; go-between; person who reconciles different parties
definitions.explanation: A person whose role is to coordinate between different parties, departments, or interests, smoothing out conflicts and finding compromises. Common in business, politics, and organizational contexts.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}が{調整役|ちょうせいやく}を{務|つと}めた。
{部署|ぶしょ}{間|かん}の{調整役|ちょうせいやく}として{活躍|かつやく}している。
examples.english: He is active as a mediator between departments.

examples.japanese: {利害|りがい}が{対立|たいりつ}する{両者|りょうしゃ}の{間|あいだ}に{立|た}ち、{調整役|ちょうせいやく}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}けることになった。
examples.english: I ended up taking on the role of mediator between the two parties whose interests were in conflict.

notes:
Composed of {調整|ちょうせい} (adjustment, coordination) and {役|やく} (role, part). Describes a specific role rather than a formal job title. Often the {調整役|ちょうせいやく} is someone who takes on this function informally because of their personality, position, or relationships.

In Japanese workplaces, the {調整役|ちょうせいやく} is a highly valued role, since consensus-building ({根回|ねまわ}し) is central to Japanese organizational culture.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {調整役|ちょうせいやく}を{務|つと}める: to serve as coordinator
- {調整役|ちょうせいやく}を{引|ひ}き{受|う}ける: to take on the role of mediator
- {調整役|ちょうせいやく}に{回|まわ}る: to take on a coordinating role
- {調整役|ちょうせいやく}として{働|はたら}く: to work as a go-between

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仲介者|ちゅうかいしゃ}: intermediary, broker — more formal, often in legal/business deals
- {仲裁者|ちゅうさいしゃ}: arbitrator — makes binding decisions in disputes
- {世話役|せわやく}: organizer, caretaker — broader; manages practical arrangements
